model_basis.generator_header: ! Mudmat / shallow-foundation screening FE — generated by digitalmodel.ansys.mudmat
model_basis.idealization: SHELL181 plate; prescribed effective-area upward pressure; six rigid modes restrained at three corners; no elastic soil stiffness or soil bearing qualification
model_basis.load: Use operative SFE/SFGRAD values, not contradictory pressure-expression comment in deck. Resultants are nominal intended values; deck decimal rounding remains part of input identity.

comparator.basis: Global equilibrium. The applied pressure field and the Meyerhof effective-area soil patch are constructed to integrate to the same force and the same moment, so the statically determinate restraints carry no load and every reaction shall vanish.
comparator.note: Verified independently of the solver by integrating the emitted pressure cards in Python: test_applied_field_integrates_to_the_applied_load reproduces both the force and the moment integrals from the numbers actually written into the deck, so the deck is not merely self-consistent with its generator.

derived_quantities.note: The effective area runs flush to the loaded edge because x_centroid + L_eff/2 = L/2 + e + (L - 2e)/2 = L identically. No additional geometry parameter is required.

input.note: This is the first value this deck has ever produced. Before #2094 it did not solve: SHELL181 accepted the subgrade modulus as a real constant and ignored it, leaving every UZ degree of freedom unrestrained.

limitations: The FE reports plate bending only. Soil bearing is not evaluated by this deck; the bearing check belongs to the geotechnical module and, for this orientation, is currently blocked by #2105.

The uniform pressure block is the bearing-capacity idealisation, not the true contact-pressure field. It is adopted so the strength check and the bearing check share one load path, at the cost of an approximate bending distribution near the patch edges. It shall not be described as contact pressure.

The peak plate stress carries no independent comparator. A rectangular plate under this load and support arrangement has no convenient closed form, so the stress magnitude is an archived run; only the equilibrium is independently established.

peak_location.note: Recorded so the peak can be distinguished from a mesh-dependent singularity.

applied_field_mesh_independence.note: Compares the emitted pressure cards at element sizes 100 and 50 mm. This guards the defect class that a mesh-convergence study would have concealed: the superseded deck's applied resultant varied as 2/(L/ESIZE + 1), so refinement changed the answer and would have been read as convergence.

bearing_cross_check.note: Recorded as unavailable rather than satisfied. A cross-check computed from a different geometry is not a cross-check.
bearing_cross_check.reason: That module applies the Meyerhof reduction to width_b_m and enforces B <= L, so it can only express eccentricity along the shorter plan dimension. This example's moment acts about the width axis, giving eccentricity along the longer dimension. Supplying the dimensions in the order its guard demands returns 8.0 m2 against a correct 9.0 m2, an 11.1 percent error, silently.

model_basis.load: Inner-wall SFL pressure plus uniform temperature

acceptance.basis: ASME VIII membrane allowable for SA-516 Gr 70 at the design temperature
acceptance.note: Peak von Mises is 51.8 percent of the 260 MPa stated yield, so the linear-elastic idealisation is comfortably inside its validity range. The superseded 30 mm parameterisation reached 99.8 percent of yield, which it was not.

comparator.exactness_note: sigma_z is exactly zero rather than approximately so. The deck applies pressure to the inner line only, with no end cap and a free top edge. For the Lame field sigma_r + sigma_theta is constant through the wall, so the axial strain is uniform and u_z = eps_zz * z satisfies the bottom-edge UY restraint identically. The restraint therefore introduces no corner disturbance and the comparison carries no idealisation error of its own.
comparator.inputs: ri = 750 mm, ro = 810 mm, P = 10 MPa
comparator.residual_note: The 0.55 percent deviation is mesh discretisation: ESIZE is wall_t/4, giving four elements through a 60 mm wall.

equilibrium.criterion: Both reactions shall be zero to solver precision. A non-zero axial reaction indicates an unintended load or restraint; a non-zero radial reaction cannot arise unless a radial restraint has been re-introduced, which is the defect this issue removed.

input.note: The generator commit is recorded separately from the deck hash. A generator change that regenerates an identical deck leaves the hash unchanged; a generator change that alters the deck invalidates this golden even though the byte-match guard would still pass, because that guard compares the deck to the generator rather than either to a comparator.

peak_location.note: Recorded so the reported peak can be distinguished from a mesh-dependent singularity. For this model the peak is the inner-fibre hoop stress, which converges; the node is captured as standing practice rather than because this case is at risk.

solver.note: The run configuration is recorded because a value reproduces only under the conditions that produced it. Distributed and iterative solvers are not bit-reproducible across core counts, so a stability comparison is valid only against a matching configuration.
